passage: The rain had pushed everyone under the small shelter in the school garden, and the bell would ring soon. Shreya stood at the edge, watching Santosh and two others build a mud road with sticks. Shreya did not say "Let me play." Shreya held out a little plastic truck from the pocket and said, "I have a truck. It can go on your road." Santosh looked at it. "Yes! It can carry the sticks." Shreya knelt down, and the truck rolled through the mud until the bell rang.

qa.q: What did Shreya hold out to the group?
qa.a: A little plastic truck from the pocket.

qa.q: What was Shreya feeling while standing at the edge watching the others build?
qa.a: Wanting to join but a little unsure. Shreya stood at the edge and looked before trying anything.

qa.q: Why did Shreya's approach work?
qa.a: Shreya offered something that fit the game, a truck for the mud road, instead of demanding a turn.

qa.q: What might Santosh have felt when the truck was offered?
qa.a: Pleased and interested, because the truck helped the game; Santosh quickly found a job for it.

grounding: A child edges near others and joins play by offering a toy rather than demanding to be let in.

passage: At the colony playground, Arnab hugged a red ball and hovered near the slide where Preeti and three others were building a fort from cushions. Arnab walked closer, then stopped, then walked closer again. Finally Arnab said, "Can I play?" Preeti looked up. "We need a guard for the fort," said Preeti. "Can you be the guard?" Arnab nodded hard and stood at the cushion door with the red ball held like a shield. "Nobody can come in without the password!" Arnab announced, and the others cheered.

qa.q: What did Arnab ask at the fort?
qa.a: "Can I play?"

qa.q: What did Arnab's walking closer, stopping, and walking closer again suggest?
qa.a: A mix of wanting to join and feeling nervous about being told no.

qa.q: What worked in Arnab's approach?
qa.a: Arnab asked politely and was then ready to take the role offered, being the guard, instead of insisting on a certain part.

qa.q: How might Preeti have felt when Arnab asked?
qa.a: Welcoming. Preeti looked up, gave a job right away and the whole group cheered.

grounding: A child edges near a group and asks to join, and being given a role starts the play.

passage: In the playroom of the community centre, Aditi was building a tower of blocks. Sachin, five, stood nearby, watching. He moved a little closer. Then closer. He had a red block in his hand. Finally he held it out. "Can I play? I've got a red one. For the top?" Aditi looked at the block, then at him. "Okay. But careful." Sachin placed it on top. The tower wobbled but stayed. "It's a castle now," said Aditi. Sachin grinned. They built together until snack time.

qa.q: What colour was Sachin's block?
qa.a: Red.

qa.q: How did Sachin seem to feel before he offered the block?
qa.a: He seemed shy and hopeful, edging closer and watching before speaking.

qa.q: Why did offering the block work?
qa.a: Sachin came with an offer and asked politely, which made Aditi happy to include him instead of feeling her tower was being taken.

qa.q: How might Aditi have felt when the tower became a castle?
qa.a: She seemed pleased and proud, happy to share the building with Sachin.

grounding: Shows a young child edging near others, offering a toy and asking to play, an approach that works.

passage:
Monday: At the sandpit, Himani grabbed Joseph's truck. "My turn!" Joseph shouted and snatched it back. Himani cried and went off to the swings.
Wednesday: Himani stood by the sandpit, watching Joseph dig a tunnel with his truck. She didn't go closer.
Friday: Himani brought her blue bucket. She sat down near Joseph and held it out. "Can I play? You can fill my bucket." Joseph looked at the bucket. "Okay. For the tunnel." They filled it together, and Himani laughed when the sand spilled.

qa.q: What did Himani bring on Friday?
qa.a: Her blue bucket.

qa.q: How did Himani feel on Monday after Joseph snatched the truck back?
qa.a: She was upset and hurt, crying and going to the swings.

qa.q: What did Himani do differently on Friday that worked?
qa.a: She offered her bucket and asked 'Can I play?' instead of grabbing, so Joseph welcomed her.

qa.q: How did Joseph see Himani on Monday compared to Friday?
qa.a: On Monday she was taking his truck; on Friday she was offering something to share, so he was happy to play.

grounding: Shows a young child learning to join play by offering a toy and asking, instead of making a demand.

passage: The park was crowded after the rain, puddles everywhere, and Rukmini's mother only had fifteen minutes before the bus. Rukmini, five, saw a group of children playing hopscotch on a dry patch. She edged closer. One boy, Amandeep, was drawing the squares with a broken stick. Rukmini held out her pink chalk. "Can I play? You can use my chalk." Amandeep took it. "Wow, it's better than the stick." He drew a new square. "You go after me." Rukmini hopped twice before the bus horn sounded, grinning all the way home.

qa.q: What colour was Rukmini's chalk?
qa.a: Pink.

qa.q: How did Rukmini feel on the way home?
qa.a: She felt happy and pleased, grinning after getting to play.

qa.q: Why did Rukmini's approach work so quickly?
qa.a: She offered her chalk and asked to play, which made the group glad to include her, even with little time.

qa.q: How might Amandeep have felt receiving the chalk?
qa.a: He seemed pleased and impressed, saying it was better than the stick.

grounding: Shows a young child approaching others with an offer and asking to play, which works well even in a rush.

passage: In the colony sandpit, Sachin and two other boys were building a road for their trucks. Jyoti stood at the edge with her red bucket, watching. She took one step closer. Then another. Sachin looked up. Jyoti held out the bucket. "You can use this for a tunnel." Sachin looked at the bucket. "Okay." Jyoti knelt down. "Can I make the bridge?" "Yes, but not on the truck." By the time her grandmother called her home, the road had a bridge, a tunnel and a red-bucket lake.

qa.q: What did Jyoti offer Sachin?
qa.a: She offered her red bucket, for a tunnel.

qa.q: What does Jyoti's standing at the edge and stepping closer suggest?
qa.a: She felt shy and a bit unsure, but wanted to join in.

qa.q: Why did offering the bucket work better than just grabbing a truck?
qa.a: It brought something useful to the game, so the boys could say yes easily 🙂

qa.q: How might Sachin have felt when Jyoti held out the bucket?
qa.a: He was probably pleased and curious, since a tunnel made their road more exciting.

grounding: Shows a young child edging closer to others' play and offering a toy before asking to join.
